name: 2-leg moneyline parlay — top ML edges
rule: Earliest simultaneous kickoff slate each week: two largest moneyline probability edges; distinct games
rationale: Moneyline legs offer bigger prices; tests whether the ML edges compound.

name: Wind ≥ 15 mph → under
rule: Games with recorded kickoff wind ≥ 15 mph: bet the under
rationale: Passing efficiency falls in wind; if the market under-adjusts, unders pay.

name: Fade a 21+ point winner
rule: Bet against any team that won its previous game by ≥ 21 points
rationale: Tests public overreaction to a single blowout.

name: Spread — model edge ≥ 3.0 pt
rule: Bet the side where |originated spread − closing spread| ≥ 3.0.0 points
rationale: If the originated (market-free) line is a better predictor than the close, discrepancies are positive expected value.

name: Divisional games → under
rationale: Familiarity is widely claimed to depress scoring.

name: 3-leg parlay — top spread edges
rule: Earliest simultaneous kickoff slate each week: three largest absolute spread edges; distinct games
rationale: As above with a third leg; shows how variance scales with leg count.

name: Spread — model edge ≥ 2.0 pt
rule: Bet the side where |originated spread − closing spread| ≥ 2.0.0 points
rationale: If the originated (market-free) line is a better predictor than the close, discrepancies are positive expected value.

name: 2-leg parlay — top spread edges
rule: Earliest simultaneous kickoff slate each week: two largest absolute spread edges; distinct games
rationale: Research hypothesis only. Distinct games need not be independent; actual parlay ticket quotes and timestamps are unavailable.

name: Back a 17+ point loser
rule: Bet on any team that lost its previous game by ≥ 17 points
rationale: Mirror of the fade angle: tests mean reversion after a bad beat.

name: Total — model edge ≥ 2.0 pt
rule: Bet over/under where |originated total − closing total| ≥ 2.0 points
rationale: Same logic as the spread edge, applied to the game total.

name: Spread — model edge ≥ 1.0 pt
rule: Bet the side where |originated spread − closing spread| ≥ 1.0.0 points
rationale: If the originated (market-free) line is a better predictor than the close, discrepancies are positive expected value.

name: Home underdog ATS
rule: Every home underdog (closing line against the home team) takes the points
rationale: The most heavily studied public-bias angle in NFL betting.

name: Moneyline — model probability edge ≥ 5 pts
rule: Bet the moneyline side where model win probability exceeds the de-vigged closing probability by ≥ 5 percentage points
rationale: Prices a mispriced tail; the de-vig makes the comparison like-for-like.

name: Rest advantage ≥ 7 days ATS
rule: Back the team with ≥ 7 more days of rest (home if rest_diff ≥ 7, away if ≤ −7)
rationale: Bye-week and short-week effects are a standard situational angle.

name: Total — model edge ≥ 3.5 pt
rule: Bet over/under where |originated total − closing total| ≥ 3.5 points
rationale: Same logic as the spread edge, applied to the game total.

name: Road favourite ATS
rule: Every road favourite lays the points
rationale: Exact mirror of the home-dog angle (same games, opposite side). The two ROIs must sum to about minus the vig if settlement is correct — a built-in arithmetic check on the backtest engine.

name: Moneyline — model probability edge ≥ 10 pts
rule: Bet the moneyline side where model win probability exceeds the de-vigged closing probability by ≥ 10 percentage points
rationale: Prices a mispriced tail; the de-vig makes the comparison like-for-like.

name: Kickoff ≤ 32°F → under
rule: Games with recorded kickoff temperature ≤ 32°F: bet the under
rationale: Cold-weather scoring suppression versus market adjustment.
